cameraRateCharacterization.method: Call actual OrbitController/AngularController/LinearController factories with identical inputs and 30/60/120/144 update counts per second. Isolated circular track removes geometric speed modulation; no global clocks or runtime code altered. This is source characterization, not a browser refresh-rate measurement.

interpretation.continuousOrbit: Discard first 500ms and frames after actual keyup. P95/P99 describe rendered intervals, not presentation latency.
interpretation.gpu: Ignore sub-0.1ms samples from idle engine frames; raw data retained. GPU timers disabled in both resolution probe variants.
interpretation.crouch: A deliberate 700ms hold includes 100ms of on-demand idle after the 600ms animation; do not call that gap a hitch.
interpretation.shot: Event-to-ball-motion includes the original power-dependent pullback and acceleration duration. Shot directions vary because orbit integration depends on frame count; results are not paired identical trajectories.
interpretation.resolution: DPR1 and DPR2 probes use the same query-free instrumentation and script, but only one round; directional evidence, not cross-device certification.

limitations: All sessions are short Practice samples. No AI timing, full-match or endurance certification.
No real 120/144Hz display measurement; rate characterization calls production factories offline.
No presented-frame timestamps or human display-ghosting assessment.
Observed views cover wide orbit arcs; do not constitute exhaustive every-angle pixel/collision validation.

findings.evidence: Actual camera factories move 40.93 degrees at 60 updates/s and 86.04 degrees at 120 updates/s for the same two-second circular-track input. Linear camera settling takes 52 updates, not a fixed duration. Aim-camera gain animation advances by a hardcoded 0.016s.
findings.recommendation: Make presentation camera integration and damping depend on elapsed time using a 60Hz reference; retain original physics, game clock and PCOL baseline. Characterize 30/60/120/144 update schedules and irregular schedules before changing feel.

findings.topic: High pixel load in new interiors
findings.evidence: 001/002 show repeated long walking frames on both browsers. Both query-free resolution probes keep all lights/materials unchanged; DPR1 substantially improves walking, aim direction changes and ball motion.
findings.recommendation: First prototype a configurable rendering pixel budget or cautiously adjusted DPR, with 1.5 as a trial value. Avoid rapid resolution oscillation. Profile shader and spatial batching costs separately before reducing scene content or lights.

findings.topic: Long aim transition and camera settling
findings.evidence: The stance-to-aim transition is configured for 1.2 seconds. Circular-track orbit release requires approximately 29 updates (~0.48s at 60Hz).
findings.recommendation: After removing update-rate dependency, trial a 0.7–0.9s aim transition and a shorter release tail as an explicit feel change, with reversible settings and behavior validation.

findings.evidence: All 20 real shots completed. Space-to-ball-motion was approximately 0.59–0.60s, consistent with the original power-dependent pullback and forward acceleration; this is not raw input latency. WorldClient already extrapolates visual ball states for fractional accumulated time.
findings.recommendation: Preserve solver and ball-state synchronization. If a quicker shot is desired, change and validate the visual cue preparation separately; do not treat it as a reason to change friction, velocity or physics step size.

findings.evidence: Gaming activates a 500ms-delayed BASIC CONTROLS dialog; GameHelp intentionally owns focus and locks the screen, interrupting input.
findings.recommendation: Consider presenting the first-use guide before active movement or requiring an explicit start/close step, preserving accessible focus handling. Do not count its intentional pause as a rendering hitch.
